formula_convention.notes: For annual accounting signals, t is the portfolio formation year. A suffix such as at_t_minus_1 refers to Compustat fiscal-year data ending in calendar year t-1, not the portfolio return year.

economic_intuition.value: Corporate asset expansion tends to be followed by abnormally low returns, while asset contraction tends to be followed by abnormally high returns; annual asset growth negatively predicts subsequent stock returns.

source.location: Abstract p.1609; Introduction pp.1609-1612
source.quote: "Asset growth rates are strong predictors of future abnormal returns."
source.interpretation: The abstract states predictive power; the introduction links asset expansion to low future returns and asset contraction to high future returns.

definition.value: Annual firm asset growth rate, defined as the year-on-year percentage change in total assets.

source.location: Section I Data p.1613; Appendix p.1648
source.quote: "the annual firm asset growth rate (ASSETG), is calculated using the year-on-year percentage change in total assets"
source.interpretation: This directly defines ASSETG as annual percentage change in total assets.

source.location: Section I Data p.1613 Equation (1); Appendix p.1648
source.quote: "ASSETG(t) = [Data6(t − 1) − Data6(t − 2)] / Data6(t − 2)"
source.interpretation: Data6 is Compustat total assets, so the machine formula is (at_t_minus_1 - at_t_minus_2) / at_t_minus_2.

calculation_steps.name: compute_asset_growth
calculation_steps.description: Compute annual percentage growth in total assets from fiscal year t-2 to fiscal year t-1.

source.location: Section I Data p.1613 Equation (1); Appendix p.1648

source.interpretation: Data6 is Compustat total assets, so the machine formula is (at_t_minus_1 - at_t_minus_2) / at_t_minus_2.

sign.meaning: High asset growth is associated with lower subsequent returns.

source.location: Introduction p.1610; Section II.A Cross-Sectional Tests p.1622; Table II Panel B Year 1
source.quote: 'we document a strong negative correlation between a firm’s asset growth and subsequent abnormal returns'
source.interpretation: This directly states the sign: higher asset growth predicts lower subsequent returns. Table II then supports it numerically with negative high-minus-low spreads for EW and VW portfolios.

implied_factor_direction.note: Paper reports high-minus-low spread comparisons but does not explicitly define a tradable simple long-short strategy. Direction is inferred for backtesting from the negative high-minus-low spread / high ASSETG -> low returns relation.

reported_results.return_type_explanation: Panel B reports average monthly raw returns to equal-weighted and value-weighted asset-growth decile portfolios. Panel C reports Fama-French three-factor monthly alphas as risk-adjusted secondary results.

comparison_policy.note: Paper reports high-minus-low spreads. If backtest constructs an implied low-minus-high factor, multiply by -1 before comparing to paper-reported spreads.

source.location: Section II.A Cross-Sectional Tests p.1622; Table II caption pp.1617-1621
source.quote: "we calculate monthly returns for EW and VW portfolios for the next 12 months"; "Panel B.1 reports average monthly raw returns ... Panel B.2 reports average monthly raw returns"
source.interpretation: The paper evaluates the main Year 1 raw-return spread using average monthly raw returns on EW and VW asset-growth decile portfolios held from July of year t to June of year t+1. Input-return components: ret_i,m: monthly stock return for firm i in month m; w_i,t: portfolio weight for value-weighted portfolios; asset_growth_decile: portfolio formed from June(t) ASSETG decile cutoffs

return_combination.note: This is the paper-reported spread direction. The implied backtest factor direction may be low-minus-high because high asset growth predicts lower returns.

annotator_notes: Main-spec timing: accounting variables are formed at end of June in year t using fiscal year-end t-1 Compustat information. Control details for BM/market value/lagged returns are relevant for multivariate tests and size groups, but ASSETG itself only needs annual total assets. Paper reports EW and VW portfolios and spread comparisons, not an explicitly named long-short trading strategy. Extractor output is paper-first only; CRSP exchange-code mapping and CRSP-Compustat merge keys are intentionally excluded and should be added later by a normalizer/lifecycle engine.
